title: The man who vowed to stop 'inhumane treatment of climbing boys'

evidence_packet.title: The man who vowed to stop 'inhumane treatment of climbing boys'
evidence_packet.lead: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
evidence_packet.summary: A blue plaque has been unveiled in Bowdon to commemorate the life and legacy of William Wood
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

title: Godmother of rock and roll's Manchester station gig honoured

evidence_packet.title: Godmother of rock and roll's Manchester station gig honoured
evidence_packet.lead: The blues guitarist and vocalist Sister Rosetta Tharpe performed at an empty station for TV
evidence_packet.summary: The blues guitarist and vocalist Sister Rosetta Tharpe performed at an empty station for TV
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with the unveiling of a blue plaque Tharpe, who influenced music legends Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley and Little Richard among others, was recording a show for Granada TV's Blues and Gospel Train, along with greats such as blues giant Muddy Waters The plaque is part of an initiative by social historian and broadcaster Karen Gabay, to place plaques across Manchester, honouring Black musicians who left a mark on the city It was unveiled by Gabay at Manchester Central Convention Complex - the former Manchester Central Railway Station - where Tharpe and fellow musicians boarded the train to take them to Whalley Range The historian explained: "She was one cool sister; that swagger, that strut, the way she played the guitar - so many people who see it for the first time are instantly taken aback."

title: 'It was hard to adjust after sleeping rough for a year'

evidence_packet.title: 'It was hard to adjust after sleeping rough for a year'
evidence_packet.lead: A man who slept rough in Manchester says the "real work" starts when people leave the streets
evidence_packet.summary: A man who slept rough in Manchester says the "real work" starts when people leave the streets
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A man who slept rough in Manchester for a year has said it was hard to adjust to sleeping in his own room after finally finding accommodation, as Andy Burnham unveiled a plan to get rough sleepers off the streets this winter Ben (not his real name) said homeless people would need a lot of support if the prime minister's vision "to get everyone in for Christmas" was to succeed "I've heard of people who did not sleep in a bed for months even when they got their own place and I can see why," he said "The real work begins when they leave the street." Burnham's plan will see emergency accommodation provided for all rough sleepers this winter to end the need for rough sleeping, alongside practical support for any health needs, as part of a £442m package Ben said he ended up living on the streets after a mental breakdown following the loss of three family members in a short period of time

title: Blackley stabbing victim 'will live forever in our hearts'

evidence_packet.title: Blackley stabbing victim 'will live forever in our hearts'
evidence_packet.lead: Kevin Lewis, also known as Abdul Kareem, died in hospital two days after being stabbed, police say
evidence_packet.summary: Kevin Lewis, also known as Abdul Kareem, died in hospital two days after being stabbed, police say
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A family has said a father-of-four who died following a stabbing "will live forever in our hearts" Kevin Lewis, also known as Abdul Kareem, died in hospital two days after police were called to a disturbance at an address in Blackley, Manchester, at about 02:45 BST on Saturday The 36-year-old was described by his family as "a devout Muslim" and "a kind and caring person whose warmth touched the hearts of everyone who knew him" A woman, 29, initially arrested on suspicion of wounding and assaulting a police officer in connection with the incident has now been arrested on suspicion of murder. She has been bailed pending further investigation Lewis's family said he was "a loving father, son, brother, uncle and dear friend" "He was a kind and caring person whose warmth touched the hearts of everyone who knew him," they said

evidence_packet.summary: Plans to transform the Grade II listed theatre into "a vibrant destination" take a step forward

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A social reformer who relentlessly campaigned against the inhumane practice of using child chimney sweeps has been honoured with a blue plaque outside his former home William Wood, who was born in 1782, was a successful wool merchant before becoming one of Britain's most determined social reformers His campaigning laid the groundwork for the Chimney Sweepers Act of 1875, which finally banned the practice, but Wood did not live to see the law enacted as he died in 1868 at the age of 85 At the plaque unveiling at his former home in Bowdon, councillor Eve Parker, from Trafford Council, said Wood's "compassion, courage and lasting impact on British history will be remembered for generations to come" "William Wood's story is a remarkable piece of local history, and it's a privilege to honour his life's work," the executive member for leisure, arts, culture and heritage said "From his home in Bowdon, he fought tirelessly against unimaginable cruelty, using his own time and resources to protect vulnerable children across the country."

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A unique slice of Manchester's musical history - when the "Godmother of rock and roll" performed live at a city railway station - has been commemorated The day Sister Rosetta Tharpe played at the disused station at Whalley Range's Wilbraham Road in May 1964 has been marked with the unveiling of a blue plaque Tharpe, who influenced music legends Chuck Berry, Elvis Presley and Little Richard among others, was recording a show for Granada TV's Blues and Gospel Train, along with greats such as blues giant Muddy Waters The plaque is part of an initiative by social historian and broadcaster Karen Gabay, to place plaques across Manchester, honouring Black musicians who left a mark on the city It was unveiled by Gabay at Manchester Central Convention Complex - the former Manchester Central Railway Station - where Tharpe and fellow musicians boarded the train to take them to Whalley Range The historian explained: "She was one cool sister; that swagger, that strut, the way she played the guitar - so many people who see it for the first time are instantly taken aback."

He was 22 and had only been in the prison and young offender institution in Bickershaw, near Wigan , for 10 days after being transferred from HMP Forest Bank in Salford The report, published by watchdog the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman after an investigation into the tragedy, said a post-mortem examination confirmed he had taken 'psychoactive substances' before his death Ombudsman Adrian Usher said: "Although this was not found to have caused his death, psychoactive substances are known to affect mental health adversely. evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Nations committee UNESCO has thrown its support behind Jodrell Bank Observatory, as funding cuts threaten the working future of its iconic Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope In a statement issued exclusively to the Manchester Evening News , the body said it was 'premature to speculate' on whether the Government's cuts could ultimately affect the observatory's coveted World Heritage status, bestowed on Jodrell Bank in 2019 due to its significance to a UNESCO said it hasn't 'officially been notified of any development' in terms of the site's future funding, but confirmed it was attempting to liaise with 'UK authorities to gather information related to the conservation, management and future use of the property' The awarding of World Heritage status - a huge coup for countries across the world - isn't decided by a site's funding model alone But, crucially in the case of Jodrell Bank, it depends on whether a site continues to be able to operate in the manner that led to the status being awarded in the first place

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Young prisoner, 22, found dead in cell just 10 days after moving into prison Dylan Woodhead wasn't checked in his cell properly the night before he was found dead after he got drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease' Comments News Paul Britton Rep A young prisoner found dead in his cell was able to obtain drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease', a watchdog said in a new report which also revealed he wasn't checked properly the night before his death Dylan Woodhead died at HMP Hindley on January 8, 2021. He was 22 and had only been in the prison and young offender institution in Bickershaw, near Wigan , for 10 days after being transferred from HMP Forest Bank in Salford The report, published by watchdog the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman after an investigation into the tragedy, said a post-mortem examination confirmed he had taken 'psychoactive substances' before his death Ombudsman Adrian Usher said: "Although this was not found to have caused his death, psychoactive substances are known to affect mental health adversely. I am concerned that Mr Woodhead was able to obtain psychoactive substances with apparent ease at Hindley, even though strict re Concerns over roll call checks at the prison have also been raised - the report reveals he wasn't checked by an officer the night before he was found dead

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Homelessness Greater Manchester will get £17million to tackle homelessness. So what should it be spent on? Charities give their verdicts, as the Prime Minister announces he wants to get people off the streets by Christmas View 9 Images News Iram Ramza As well as his insistence that he would bring the welfare down and honour the UK’s defence commitments abroad, his first pledge was to tackle the homelessness crisis “I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction – to end rough sleeping in our country. It’s about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government,” he told the nation. “I will put the care of people at the heart of everythin Some £340 million funding was announced to go towards acquiring suitable homes, identifying those most in need and starting to provide housing and support ‘without delay’ The funding will provide 1,200 homes and intensive support for at least 3,000 long-term rough sleepers over a five-year period, the Government said The latest annual national statistics, published by the Government in February, estimated that 4,793 people were sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025 in England. That was a new record and the fourth annual increase in a row

title: The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance

evidence_packet.summary: NHS The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue. Betha Comments News Bethan Finighan Science and Innovation Writer and Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 18:29, 19 Aug 2026 Dozens of patients died or ‘came to harm’ due to treatment delays and serious errors made by staff working under extreme pressure at a Greater Manchester hospi Lengthy delays were linked with ‘28 deaths’ and 56 issues of ‘severe harm’, while problems diagnosing illness led to ten deaths last year at the Northern Care Alliance (NCA) which treats more than a million patients at hospitals in Salford , Oldham , Bury and Rochdale There were ten ‘never events’ recorded at the NCA across 2025 and 2026, which the NHS describes as patient safety incidents which were ‘wholly preventable,’ according to the trust’s own reports Concerns were also raised with maternity care, with reports highlighting an issue with increasing numbers of stillbirths recorded earlier this year There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue

title: Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status

evidence_packet.title: Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status
evidence_packet.lead: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Natio
evidence_packet.summary: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Natio
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Nations committee UNESCO has thrown its support behind Jodrell Bank Observatory, as funding cuts threaten the working future of its iconic Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope In a statement issued exclusively to the Manchester Evening News , the body said it was 'premature to speculate' on whether the Government's cuts could ultimately affect the observatory's coveted World Heritage status, bestowed on Jodrell Bank in 2019 due to its significance to a UNESCO said it hasn't 'officially been notified of any development' in terms of the site's future funding, but confirmed it was attempting to liaise with 'UK authorities to gather information related to the conservation, management and future use of the property' The awarding of World Heritage status - a huge coup for countries across the world - isn't decided by a site's funding model alone But, crucially in the case of Jodrell Bank, it depends on whether a site continues to be able to operate in the manner that led to the status being awarded in the first place

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Purple Lamborghini seized by police after supercar driver's 'excessive engine revving' GMP said new powers are now available for police on the ground to prevent nusiance driving Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 16:13, 19 Aug 2026 View Image A Lamborghini supercar was taken away on the back of a truck after the driver's 'excessive revving'. Police seized the purple vehicle under new legislation to prevent anti-social behaviour involving vehicles Cops swooped to stop the purple-coloured Lamborghini Huracan on Featherstall Road in Oldham on Tuesday, Greater Manchester Police said The force said that under the new legislation, it was seized for 'anti-social driving and excessive engine revving'. An image of the sports car being loaded away was also released Under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002, as amended by the Crime and Policing Act 2026, police can now seize a vehicle immediately without first issuing a warning if the legal grounds are met Previously, a warning was generally required before seizure, GMP said

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Man accused of murdering woman found dead in Rochdale flat pleads not guilty Kyle Howard is due to go on trial in November News Andrew Bardsley Court reporter 15:51, 19 Aug 2026 View Image Keeley Aspinall (Image: GMP/family handout) A man has denied murdering a woman who was found dead in a flat in Rochdale Kyle Howard, 26, is accused of murdering 44-year-old Keeley Aspinall, who was found in an address on the town’s Freehold estate on May 25. He pleaded not guilty to the single charge Mr Howard, of Tweedale Street, Rochdale, is now set to go on trial in November. He was remanded in custody by Judge Suzanne Goddard KC A further pre-trial hearing was scheduled for October. The prosecution was represented by Rachel Faux, and the defence by Dan Gaskell during today's (August 19) hearing at Manchester Crown Court Police were called to reports of a concern for a welfare at the property off Tweedale Street. Ms Aspinall, known to friends as Kiki, was pronounced dead at the scene

evidence_packet.evidence_text: GCSE results LIVE Updated 1 min ago GCSE Results Day 2026 LIVE as grades released for students Results and reaction from schools across the region as students find out their GCSE grades Students across Greater Manchester open their GCSE results ( Imag On Thursday (August 20), 15 and 16-year-olds who sat their exams in May and June will learn whether they got the grades they needed for A levels, T levels, BTECs or apprenticeships While many students will be able to collect their results online for the first time this year, pupils are still encouraged to go to schools if they can The results were made available to schools on Wednesday (August 19) and will be available to collect from your school from 8am. title: Young prisoner, 22, found dead in cell just 10 days after moving into prison

evidence_packet.title: Young prisoner, 22, found dead in cell just 10 days after moving into prison
evidence_packet.lead: Wigan Young prisoner, 22, found dead in cell just 10 days after moving into prison Dylan Woodhead wasn't checked in his cell properly the night before he was found dead after he got drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease' Comments News Paul Britton Rep A young prisoner found dead
evidence_packet.summary: Wigan Young prisoner, 22, found dead in cell just 10 days after moving into prison Dylan Woodhead wasn't checked in his cell properly the night before he was found dead after he got drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease' Comments News Paul Britton Rep A young prisoner found dead
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Wigan Young prisoner, 22, found dead in cell just 10 days after moving into prison Dylan Woodhead wasn't checked in his cell properly the night before he was found dead after he got drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease' Comments News Paul Britton Rep A young prisoner found dead in his cell was able to obtain drugs behind bars with 'apparent ease', a watchdog said in a new report which also revealed he wasn't checked properly the night before his death Dylan Woodhead died at HMP Hindley on January 8, 2021. He was 22 and had only been in the prison and young offender institution in Bickershaw, near Wigan , for 10 days after being transferred from HMP Forest Bank in Salford The report, published by watchdog the Prisons and Probation Ombudsman after an investigation into the tragedy, said a post-mortem examination confirmed he had taken 'psychoactive substances' before his death Ombudsman Adrian Usher said: "Although this was not found to have caused his death, psychoactive substances are known to affect mental health adversely. I am concerned that Mr Woodhead was able to obtain psychoactive substances with apparent ease at Hindley, even though strict re Concerns over roll call checks at the prison have also been raised - the report reveals he wasn't checked by an officer the night before he was found dead

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Homelessness Greater Manchester will get £17million to tackle homelessness. So what should it be spent on? Charities give their verdicts, as the Prime Minister announces he wants to get people off the streets by Christmas View 9 Images News Iram Ramza As well as his insistence that he would bring the welfare down and honour the UK’s defence commitments abroad, his first pledge was to tackle the homelessness crisis “I will soon go through that door behind me and issue my first instruction – to end rough sleeping in our country. It’s about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government,” he told the nation. “I will put the care of people at the heart of everythin Some £340 million funding was announced to go towards acquiring suitable homes, identifying those most in need and starting to provide housing and support ‘without delay’ The funding will provide 1,200 homes and intensive support for at least 3,000 long-term rough sleepers over a five-year period, the Government said The latest annual national statistics, published by the Government in February, estimated that 4,793 people were sleeping rough on a single night in autumn 2025 in England. That was a new record and the fourth annual increase in a row

title: The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance

evidence_packet.title: The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance
evidence_packet.lead: NHS The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA.
evidence_packet.summary: NHS The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue
evidence_packet.evidence_text: NHS The human cost of a hospital trust under pressure: 28 deaths linked to delays at Northern Care Alliance There were 12,000 cases of delayed treatment last year at the NCA. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue. Bosses say ‘persistently high’ levels of sick leave are a major issue

title: Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status

evidence_packet.title: Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status
evidence_packet.lead: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Natio
evidence_packet.summary: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Natio
evidence_packet.evidence_text: The University of Manchester Survival of iconic Lovell Telescope is key, UNESCO says as funding cuts could threaten Jodrell Bank World Heritage status Sign the Manchester Evening News campaign to save the working future of the Lovell Telescope Comment The influential United Nations committee UNESCO has thrown its support behind Jodrell Bank Observatory, as funding cuts threaten the working future of its iconic Grade I-listed Lovell Telescope In a statement issued exclusively to the Manchester Evening News , the body said it was 'premature to speculate' on whether the Government's cuts could ultimately affect the observatory's coveted World Heritage status, bestowed on Jodrell Bank in 2019 due to its significance to a UNESCO said it hasn't 'officially been notified of any development' in terms of the site's future funding, but confirmed it was attempting to liaise with 'UK authorities to gather information related to the conservation, management and future use of the property' The awarding of World Heritage status - a huge coup for countries across the world - isn't decided by a site's funding model alone But, crucially in the case of Jodrell Bank, it depends on whether a site continues to be able to operate in the manner that led to the status being awarded in the first place

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Oldham Purple Lamborghini seized by police after supercar driver's 'excessive engine revving' GMP said new powers are now available for police on the ground to prevent nusiance driving Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 16:13, 19 Aug 2026 View Image A Lamborghini supercar was taken away on the back of a truck after the driver's 'excessive revving'. Police seized the purple vehicle under new legislation to prevent anti-social behaviour involving vehicles Cops swooped to stop the purple-coloured Lamborghini Huracan on Featherstall Road in Oldham on Tuesday, Greater Manchester Police said The force said that under the new legislation, it was seized for 'anti-social driving and excessive engine revving'. An image of the sports car being loaded away was also released Under Section 59 of the Police Reform Act 2002, as amended by the Crime and Policing Act 2026, police can now seize a vehicle immediately without first issuing a warning if the legal grounds are met Previously, a warning was generally required before seizure, GMP said

The 15-hour, yellow warning comes into effect at 7pm this evening (August 19), running through to 10am on Thursday morning Forecasters say heavy showers and thunderstorms are 'likely to lead to some travel disruption and flash flooding'. The warning covers all of Greater Manchester, Lancashire, Merseyside and Cumbria, plus most of Cheshire, Yorkshire, the North East and North Wales A Met Office spokesperson said: "Heavy showers will develop this evening, becoming more frequent and widespread overnight. These are likely to bring 15 to 20 mm in an hour in some areas with as much as 30 to 50 mm falling in a period of six hours in some places "These accumulations may lead to a few places seeing some flooding. Alongside the rain, some showers are likely to be thundery, bringing the additional hazards of lightning and hail. The showers will ease from the northwest Thursday morning." Rail disruption, power supply issues and damage to buildings could also be caused by the storm, the Met Office says

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester United’s 2026/27 match shirt starts the season with Snapdragon across the chest. That part isn’t new. What changed is the rule around it: after the 2025/26 season, Premier League clubs stopped selling the front of their matchday shirts to gambling companies At almost the same moment, Canada moved the other way. Alberta opened its regulated competitive iGaming market on July 13, 2026, joining Ontario, whose market has been open since April 4, 2022. A United supporter in Canada can now watch a league reducing one of football’s most vi That creates an unusual setup for anyone following United and soccer betting from Canada. The shirt looks cleaner, but the commercial relationship hasn’t vanished. The match is the same while the betting menu can change with a provincial border In April 2023, Premier League clubs collectively agreed to remove gambling sponsorship from the front of matchday shirts after the 2025/26 season. The measure was voluntary and narrow. It applies to the front of the playing shirt, not to every place a betting company can appear a Sleeves can still carry commercial branding. Training wear remains available. Stadium boards and digital content weren’t swept away by the front-of-shirt agreement. The difference matters because 11 of the 20 Premier League clubs entered 2025/26 with gambling brands on the front Many clubs that had relied on betting money for their most valuable shirt position needed replacements at the same time, while betting companies looked for other inventory that still delivered global football exposure

Many of these items contain batteries and valuable materials that can be recover When electrical items are placed in black and brown bins, they can also become damaged during collection and processing. This can cause batteries to spark, leading to fires that put waste and recycling crews at risk and can cause significant damage to vehicles and facilities Councillor Paul Kenny, portfolio holder for planning, environmental services and transport, said: "We know that during periods of hot weather, fans are often essential items to help people cool down, but when these products reach the end of their life, they should never be thrown "Electrical items and batteries can cause fires if damaged, putting our collection crews and staff at risk. By taking unwanted electricals to the correct recycling point, residents can help protect our workers, reduce waste, and ensure valuable materials are recovered and reused

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new exhibition coming to The Portico Library explores feminist themes of wellbeing, ageing and place in relation to magic and ritual healing Opening this October, Witches & Healers draws on Rosie Reed Hillman’s groundbreaking project Something That Was Ours , which explores what it means to be a witch today Hillman’s portraits of witches and healers are curated in dialogue with historic texts chosen by critical friends who identify with the practice of witchcraft and/or healing. The portraits, the books chosen, and their interpretation offer unique insights into the diverse lives an Using a mix of moving image and photography, the artwork builds a sensory and emotive portrait of women in midlife. Covering themes of menopause, mental health, climate change, and marital breakdown, this work explores the ways women have reclaimed the word witch and sought solac Speaking about the exhibition , Rosie Reed Hillman says: “I have worked to build rapport with contributors over the last four years and believe the intimate access conveyed in this project creates an exhibition that inspires empathy, curiosity and a greater understanding of issue “Women in midlife of all backgrounds are an overlooked demographic who want to see art and hear stories that reflect their experiences, and I hope this work speaks to them especially.”

evidence_packet.evidence_text: GCSE results How footballers did in their GCSE exams, including Wayne Rooney, Steven Gerrard, Frank Lampard and more Some of the Premier League's best players have taken on the exams News Liam De Brun TV and Celebrity writer 06:00, 20 Aug 2026 View 8 Images Wayne Roo Over five million teenagers are collecting their grades today as GCSE results for 2026 are announced, but how did some of the nation’s best footballers do in their exams? Students are waiting to find out what they will be doing for the next stage of their education, just a week after the A-Level results were released. The bulk of the nation can remember a summer spent worrying out how our GCSEs went GCSE results will be published from 8am (GMT) on Thursday (August 20). Students will usually receive their results in one of four ways: collection in person from school, email, an online results portal or through a dedicated results app The old A* - G GCSE grading system was replaced by a 9-1 grading scale, with 9 being the highest grade and 1 being the lowest. Fully implemented in 2020, the change was intended to make it easier for sixth forms, universities and employers to distinguish between candidates Despite finding fame at a young age, it didn’t stop some of the Premier League’s best ever footballers from having to do their exams. Due to the unpredictable nature of football, an education is vital even if you’re primed to be the next Lionel Messi
